known_facts_book1: An enormous purple stone castle in a cup-shaped valley of the Gillikin Country, with no turrets or towers and one small window and one big door on each side.
Bears the words 'YOOP CASTLE' engraved over the doorway; its latch is so high that Woot must stand on the Tin Woodman's shoulders to reach it.
Was the home of Mr. Yoop the giant, and is now run by his wife to suit herself.
Its doors close of their own accord and can be opened only by a spoken command from whoever wears the **Magic Lace Apron** — nothing else will move them.
Its great hall is lined with plates of polished gold and lit without any visible lamp; furniture appears and disappears at a clap of the Giantess's hands.
In this Valley, Mrs. Yoop says, no one ever dies.
Is escaped from once, by Woot stealing the Apron in the dark, and Mrs. Yoop is later seen back in the great hall weaving a replacement.

known_relations_book1.Woot: Who steals the Apron and locks her in her own bedroom.
known_relations_book1.Polychrome: Who was caged in its bedroom for weeks.

known_facts_book1: A vast circular clearing deep in a Gillikin forest, roofed over by the top branches of tall trees and glowing with a soft white light from no visible source.
Is announced by a sign on the path warning all strangers not to follow it.
Is the whole world of the Loons, who cannot get out of the enclosure and so can harm no one who does not come to them.
Holds a throne with a string running up to the dome, so the King can be pulled down and tied in.
Has a pump for re-inflating punctured Loons, wheeled out in front of the throne when needed.

known_relations_book1.Woot: The visitor whose thorn empties half of it.

known_facts_book1: A streak of the Munchkin plain whose magic quality makes everyone within it invisible — even fairies fall under the charm.
The grass, the flowers, the plain and Mount Munch in the distance all remain visible; only the travellers cannot see themselves or one another.
Is crossed by holding hands in a line and walking toward Mount Munch, with Woot whistling so Polychrome can find him.
Is where the two tin men collide, denting the Tin Woodman's side and bending the Tin Soldier's right leg — damage they discover only on leaving it.
Is the hunting ground of the Hip-po-gy-raf, who tracks by smell because nothing there can be seen.
Is avoided entirely on the return journey, at the Scarecrow's urging.

known_relations_book1.the Hip-po-gy-raf: The beast that hunts in it.

not_in_this_book: the Invisible Country is inhabited by people

hallucination_signals: they return through the Invisible Country

known_facts_book1: A circular wall of air made hard by powerful sorcery, six feet thick and perhaps a mile high, surrounding Nimmie Amee's house at the foot of Mount Munch.
Is entirely invisible, so it does not mar the beauty of the landscape, and yet keeps all strangers away.
Was built by **Nimmie Amee herself**, using the one magic formula she carried away from the Witch's house.
Cannot be climbed, pushed through or walked around to any entrance — the circle has none.
Is passed only by shrinking small enough to use the Blue Rabbit's burrow, which runs underneath it.

known_relations_book1.Nimmie Amee: Who built it and lives at its centre.
known_relations_book1.Polychrome: Who shrinks the party to use the burrow.

known_facts_book1: The back part of Ku-Klip's dark blue house at the far edge of the great Munchkin forest, facing the plains eastward, with a lean-to addition for more room.
Holds hammers, anvils, soldering irons, a charcoal furnace, two work-benches, a long table and scraps of tin of all shapes and sizes.
Contains the **barrel in the corner** where every meat part cut from Nick Chopper and Captain Fyter was saved.
Contains the **cupboards** where the heads were kept, and where the Tin Woodman finds his own old Head still alive on a shelf.
Is where both tin men were made, and where Chopfyt was later glued together from the leftovers.
Captain Fyter opens every cupboard door looking for his own old head and finds none — it is on Chopfyt.

known_relations_book1.Ku-Klip: Its owner and the maker of everything in it.
known_relations_book1.Tin Woodman: Who says it seems almost like home to him.
known_relations_book1.the old Head: Which lives on a cupboard shelf there.
